Zarhites
ZAR-hytes
n. (the clan descended from Zerah, son of Judah, that produced Achan's judgment and two of David's mighty men)
Hebrew Zarchi (H2227), from Zerach (Zerah), a son of Judah and Tamar; the -ite suffix marking clan membership.

Biblical Definition

The Zarhites take their name from Zerah, one of the twin sons Tamar bore to Judah (Genesis 38:30), and their clan appears twice in Scripture at moments of sharp contrast — disgrace and distinguished valor. The census of Judah names them among the tribe’s major divisions: “of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites” (Numbers 26:20). Their most infamous hour comes at Ai, where Joshua, seeking the sinner whose theft of the devoted things had brought defeat on Israel, narrows the search “family by family” — “he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken” (Joshua 7:17), the process that exposed Achan, Zabdi’s own grandson, as the man whose sin had brought a curse on the whole camp. Centuries later, under David, two of the kingdom’s most formidable mighty men come from this same disgraced clan, redeeming its name in valorous service: “Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zarhites” commanded twenty-four thousand men as the eighth monthly captain (1 Chronicles 27:11), and “Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites” commanded an equal division as the tenth (1 Chronicles 27:13) — a single family line running from the shame of Achan’s theft at Ai to two captains of thousands guarding David’s throne.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Zarhites; they are the clan of Zerah son of Judah, the family from which the sinner Achan was exposed at Ai and, generations later, two of David's mighty captains descended.

expand to see more

ZARHITES, n. A family of the tribe of Judah, descended from Zerah, prominent both in Achan's exposure and in David's mighty men.

ZERAH, n. A son of Judah by Tamar, twin brother of Pharez, ancestor of the Zarhite clan.

ACHAN, n. An Israelite of the tribe of Judah, of the Zarhite family, whose theft of devoted things brought judgment on Israel at Ai.

MIGHTY MEN, n. In Scripture, the title given to David's elite warriors, renowned for individual feats of valor and loyalty.

DEVOTED THING, n. In the Mosaic law, an object placed under a ban, wholly given over to the LORD and forbidden to private use.

Key Scripture

Numbers 26:20 — "And the sons of Judah after their families were; of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites: of Pharez, the family of the Pharzites: of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites."

Joshua 7:17 — "And he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken:"

1 Chronicles 27:11 — "The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zarhites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand."

1 Chronicles 27:13 — "The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand."

Modern Corruption

A single clan name tracked with narrative consistency from Genesis through Joshua into the David narratives, disgraced in one generation and honored in another, is exactly the kind of coherent, multi-book family memory a piecemeal legendary tradition rarely sustains.

expand to see more

Fragmentary source theories that treat Joshua's conquest narrative and Chronicles' court records as unrelated literary strata, compiled by different hands with no access to each other, are hard pressed to explain the seamless clan continuity here — the same Zarhite family name, correctly nested within Judah, correctly tied to Zerah, appears with total consistency across three separate books spanning Israel's history from Moses to David.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that neither individual sin nor family shame is the final word over a covenant line: Achan's theft brought death on himself and grief on Israel (Joshua 7:24–26), yet the very same clan, generations later, produced men whose valor is recorded among David's finest — a family's history under the LORD's covenant is never simply determined by its worst hour, and grace can raise up faithfulness from the same root that once bore judgment.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Zarchi (H2227), from Zerach (H2226), Zerah, rising light; cherem (H2764), devoted thing, ban; gibbor (H1368), mighty man.

expand to see more

Hebrew Zarchi (H2227) — Zarhite, from the ancestor Zerah.

Hebrew Zerach (H2226) — Zerah, meaning rising or shining, the twin brother of Pharez.

Hebrew cherem (H2764) — devoted thing, the ban; the very thing Achan of this clan stole.

Hebrew gibbor (H1368) — mighty man; the title given to Sibbecai and Maharai, generations later.

Hebrew lakad (H3920) — to take, capture, seize by lot; the verb of Joshua's search that exposed Zabdi's house.

Usage

"“Of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites” — their place in the census of Judah."

"“He took the family of the Zarhites... and Zabdi was taken” — the search that exposed Achan."

"“Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zarhites” — the clan's later honor among David's captains."
